signals.name: prod_request_trend_28d
signals.definition: Requests in the last 28 days (2025-02-15..03-14) vs the prior 28 (2025-01-18..02-14) on production-named projects, NFR excluded. growing >= +15%, declining <= -15%, called only if prior-28 >= 100 requests.
signals.logic: WITH proj AS (SELECT id, CASE WHEN name LIKE '%-staging%' OR name LIKE '%-qa%' OR name LIKE '%-internal%' OR name LIKE '%-sandbox%' OR name LIKE '%-test%' OR name LIKE '%-trial%' OR name LIKE '%-eval%' THEN 'nonprod' ELSE 'prod' END cls FROM projects) SELECT u.customer_id, SUM(CASE WHEN u.event_date BETWEEN '2025-02-15' AND '2025-03-14' THEN u.quantity ELSE 0 END) l28, SUM(CASE WHEN u.event_date BETWEEN '2025-01-18' AND '2025-02-14' THEN u.quantity ELSE 0 END) p28 FROM usage_events u JOIN proj p ON p.id=u.project_id WHERE u.event_type='request' AND u.is_nfr=0 AND p.cls='prod' GROUP BY 1;  -- change = l28/p28-1; sum over the account's matched customers
signals.differentiates: Yes. Customer-level changes are trimodal (about -30%, 0%, +40%) with almost nothing between -20..-10% and +10..+30%, so the 15% cut is robust. Calendar weeks (wk8-11 vs wk4-7) give the same class for 143/146 customers.
signals.notes: Book-wide baseline is +3.9%. Rolling 7-day windows anchored on the reference date avoid the 6-day partial week and the weekday effect. Trends are assigned per project (within-customer project trends are independent), so 1:N accounts can hide opposite stories.

signals.name: name_classifier_impact
signals.definition: How much excluding non-prod-named projects changes each account's numbers versus trusting environment_type.
signals.logic: Same query with p.cls='prod' replaced by u.environment_type='PRODUCTION' (trusting the label). No prod-named project is SANDBOX-labelled, so the name filter alone defines production.
signals.differentiates: Material: class changes for 66 of 184 resolvable accounts (44 lose all production usage); median trend shift 0.3 pp but p90 24 pp.
signals.notes: Per-project volumes and trend mixes are statistically the same for prod- and non-prod-named projects, so this is a business rule, not something the data proves. Show both numbers when they differ.

signals.name: tokens_transcribe_agreement
signals.definition: Do tokens and transcribe (same windows, same project filter) move in the same class as requests?
signals.logic: Same query with event_type IN ('tokens','transcribe'); classify with the same +/-15% cut; agreement = same class.
signals.differentiates: As a confidence modifier, not a flag: tokens agree on 117/129 (r = 0.88), transcribe on 100/129 (r = 0.69, lower volume).
signals.notes: When all three agree, state the trend with high confidence; the 6 'neither agrees' accounts are mostly low-volume or near the 15% cut.

signals.name: contract_runway
signals.definition: balance_pct = balance/amount; linear burn = (amount-balance)/days since starting_at; projected exhaustion = today + balance/burn; compare with ending_before. Low balance = <=15% (credit, postpaid) or <=20% (prepaid), the thresholds from alerts.
signals.logic: SELECT customer_id, type, balance/amount pct, (amount-balance)/(julianday('2025-03-14')-julianday(substr(starting_at,1,10))) burn, balance/((amount-balance)/(julianday('2025-03-14')-julianday(substr(starting_at,1,10)))) days_left_at_burn, julianday(substr(ending_before,1,10))-julianday('2025-03-14') days_to_end FROM contracts;
signals.differentiates: Low balance yes (10 accounts). 'Exhausts before end' flags 65 of 114 contracts (57%), too broad on its own; the 60-day version (29) is usable.
signals.notes: Balances do not reconcile with usage: implied burn/day vs requests/day r = -0.04, consumed share vs elapsed term r = 0.08. Present balance % as a stated fact and the runway as an assumption. acc_007 IronwoodHealth: prepaid 12.5% left, runs out about 2025-04-08 vs end 2025-06-12, usage +47%.

signals.name: days_to_contract_end_or_renewal
signals.definition: ending_before - today (analytics) and, for won opps, closeDate - today (CRM renewal date).
signals.logic: julianday(substr(ending_before,1,10)) - julianday('2025-03-14'); API: opportunities[status='won'].closeDate - 2025-03-14.
signals.notes: The two dates disagree (median 77 days apart; equal on 1 of 80 pairs). No contract ends within 30 days. Show both and say which source.

signals.name: new_projects_30d
signals.definition: Projects whose created_at (or first usage) is within 30 days of today.
signals.logic: SELECT customer_id, name FROM projects WHERE created_at >= '2025-02-12'  vs  first usage: SELECT project_id, MIN(event_date) FROM usage_events GROUP BY 1 HAVING MIN(event_date) >= '2025-02-12';
signals.differentiates: Doesn't hold up as defined: created_at flags 25 accounts, but usage predates created_at on every project created in the window. By first usage, only acc_005's '-eval' project is new (first used 2025-03-08).
signals.notes: Named projects like -new, -launch, -api, -coding, -clinical look like intended expansion stories; if used, call them 'project metadata says new' with low confidence.

signals.name: tenant_started_recently
signals.definition: Customer created_at (= first usage) after the window start.
signals.logic: SELECT id, created_at FROM customers WHERE created_at > '2024-12-15T08:00:00.000Z';  -- plus dormant tenants whose first usage is recent
signals.differentiates: Yes, specific: acc_001, acc_036, acc_109, acc_151, acc_182, acc_188 onboarding, plus acc_005 (dormant closed_lost tenant woke up 2025-03-08). cust_206 has no CRM account.
signals.notes: The only >=2x jumps over the trailing 4-week mean in the whole dataset are onboarding ramps (cust_001, cust_035, cust_108); the usage_spike alert never fired.

signals.name: api_key_changes
signals.definition: Keys created in the last 30 days; inactive keys.
signals.logic: SELECT customer_id, SUM(created_at >= '2025-02-12'), SUM(active=0) FROM api_keys GROUP BY 1;
signals.differentiates: No. Same rate on growing (52%), flat (45%) and declining (60%) accounts. Dropped.
signals.notes: 12% of keys were last used before they were created; 'active' only encodes last use within 30 days; no deactivation date.

signals.name: pre_customer_sandbox
signals.definition: Accounts in prospect/evaluation/mvp whose tenant has SANDBOX-labelled usage (or only non-prod-named usage).
signals.logic: SELECT customer_id, SUM(quantity) FROM usage_events WHERE environment_type='SANDBOX' AND event_type='request' AND is_nfr=0 GROUP BY 1;  + CRM stage IN (prospect, evaluation, mvp)
signals.differentiates: SANDBOX version is very specific: acc_002 ($742k eval, ~6 req/week trial), acc_006 ($87k eval, sandbox+test growing +38-46%), acc_008 ($1.02M mvp closing 2025-04-13, 2-5 req/week). The name-only version (27) is broad.
signals.notes: cust_006 and cust_008 also hold credit contracts with fired credit_low alerts, which contradicts 'pre-customer'.

signals.name: noncustomer_usage
signals.definition: Prospect/closed_lost accounts with production-named usage, and the subset with growing usage.
signals.logic: stage IN ('prospect','closed_lost') AND prod l28 > 0 (any) / AND trend class = growing.
signals.differentiates: 'Any usage' does not: every matched prospect and closed_lost tenant uses the product daily. 'Growing' does (12: acc_003, 017, 037, 057, 085, 099, 118, 126 prospects; acc_033, 046, 106, 124 closed_lost).
signals.notes: Treat as 'CRM stage is probably stale', i.e. a hygiene or upsell conversation, not proof of a deal.

signals.name: days_since_contact
signals.definition: today - account.lastContactAt.
signals.logic: API: 2025-03-14 - accounts[].lastContactAt (do not use contacts.lastContactedAt, a copy).
signals.differentiates: Moderately: customers 0-20 days, evaluation/mvp 0-30, prospects 0-69, closed_lost 45-298. >14 days flags 39% of active-stage accounts; use as a tiebreaker.
signals.notes: Only 1-3 activities per account, so recency is coarse.

signals.name: meeting_outcome_and_notes
signals.definition: Latest meeting outcome and note text from activities.
signals.logic: API: GET /accounts/:id/activities -> type='meeting' (outcome), type='note' (text).
signals.differentiates: Yes but tiny coverage: 8 accounts in total. Highest-precision qualitative evidence (acc_022 negative meeting + dissatisfaction note on -28% usage).
signals.notes: Meetings carry no attendee (contactIds always []). Notes older than the usage window (acc_003, acc_005) still explain context.

signals.name: open_opportunity_value_and_close
signals.definition: Open opp value and days to its closeDate.
signals.logic: API: GET /accounts/:id/opportunities -> status='open' -> value, closeDate - 2025-03-14.
signals.differentiates: Yes. 18 deals ($5.19M) close within 45 days; combined with engagement it isolates acc_002 and acc_008 (big deals, near-zero product use).
signals.notes: Don't use account.opportunityAmount for this (it also carries won renewals).

signals.name: stage_vs_reality
signals.definition: CRM stage contradicted by analytics: prospect/closed_lost with a contract, customer without contract or without production usage.
signals.logic: stage vs (contract exists) vs (prod-named l28 > 0).
signals.differentiates: Weak on its own: contract presence is independent of stage (62% of prospects, 46% of closed_lost, 59% of customers have one), so these are mostly generator noise. Useful as hygiene notes or when combined with a usage trend.
signals.notes: Strongest specific cases: acc_003 and acc_017 (prospects with contracts, growing usage, notes saying 'no deal'/'low priority'), acc_005 (closed_lost with contract and reactivated usage).

signals.name: declining_near_renewal
signals.definition: Customer with declining production usage and a renewal (won-opp closeDate) or contract end within 75 days.
signals.logic: trend class = declining AND stage='customer' AND min(days_to_won_close, days_to_contract_end) <= 75.
signals.differentiates: Yes: acc_009, acc_022, acc_023, acc_127, acc_187.
signals.notes: Highest-urgency retention list; acc_022 also has the only negative meeting.

signals.definition: model_name / route / agent_used / language_used / source mix per customer, shift between first and last 4 full weeks, breadth.

join.method: No shared key. Normalise CRM name (drop Group/LLC/Ltd/Inc/Healthcare and ' - North/West', keep [a-z0-9]) and domain (drop .example, keep [a-z0-9]); normalise analytics customer_name (drop -prod|prod|-cloud|-trial|-us|-eu|-sandbox|-holdings|-health-group), domain (drop .example and trailing 'customers') and billing-email domain. Candidate = any equal key. notes: Disambiguators tested and rejected: created_at gap (random, -638..+769 days, 58% positive), region (no CRM counterpart), owner_email (role mailboxes), stage vs contract presence (independent), contract ending_before vs opp closeDate (median 77 days apart), opp value vs contract amount (r = 0.12).

Generator artefact (not a key): ids are ordinally aligned. acc_N = cust_N for N<=10, acc_011 = cust_011+012, acc_012/013 = cust_013/014, acc_014/015 have no tenant, acc_N = cust_(N-1) for N>=16. All 183 unambiguous matches agree with it (100% precision check). It also implies the pairing in id_order_hint. Use it only to validate, never as a production join rule.

Within clusters the candidates differ materially (e.g. VeridianSleep: one tenant flat with no contract, the other +34% with a prepaid contract), so a wrong guess would mislead. The preview leaves usage fields empty for the 16 ambiguous accounts and lists each candidate in candidates_summary.

The 7 duplicate clusters cannot be separated with legitimate fields (created_at, region, owner_email, contracts, opp dates/amounts all tested). Only the generator's ordinal id pattern separates them, which is an artefact.

environment_type: 49.8% of PRODUCTION-labelled request volume (50.6% tokens, 49.8% transcribe) comes from non-prod-named projects - but the names are staging/qa/internal/sandbox(+2/3). The single '-test' project is SANDBOX-labelled, and 18 of 19 '-sandbox' projects are labelled PRODUCTION. Prod- and non-prod-named projects have the same volume and trend distributions, so the name rule is a business assumption the data cannot confirm.

Sandbox-only tenants cust_002/006/008 -> acc_002/006/008 holds. Nuance: only their projects (and cust_006's customer row) say SANDBOX; cust_006 and cust_008 also have credit contracts ($117.9k, $232.5k) and fired credit_low alerts.

Alert history: '~23 fired with >50% balance' is exactly 23/35. Stronger: only 1 of 35 (cust_040, 16.8% vs 0.20) fired at or below its threshold; 9 customers at/below threshold never fired; credit_low also fires on 10 postpaid contracts; usage_spike never fired.
Persona vs title: technical titles always map to 'technical'. Only the 11 non-technical titles get a random executive/clinical/operations persona.
Activities: 198 accounts have 1-3, but acc_014 and acc_015 have none. The 2 email subjects are fully determined by direction.
Tasks: 152/161 open tasks overdue holds; the other 9 are due today, and no task in the CRM is due after 2025-03-14.
Account opportunityAmount/closeDate mirror the opp (135/135, plus nextStep 135/135). They mirror won renewals too, so opportunityAmount is not 'open value' as the docs say.

Usage dimensions are not uniform: each follows a fixed per-event-type mix (e.g. language always empty on tokens; transcribe models only on transcribe). Within event type they are independent of customer and time, so DROP stands.
Constant/empty columns all confirmed. Additions: tasks.description 100% NULL, alert_status constant, and projects.created_at is contradicted by usage on every in-window project.
'Usage on closed_lost/prospect accounts' is universal (every matched tenant has daily usage), so on its own it is not a signal. Only the growing subset (12 accounts) or reactivation (acc_005) is.
caveats: Reference date 2025-03-14 ('today'). Windows are rolling 7-day weeks anchored on it (L28 = 02-15..03-14, P28 = 01-18..02-14), which avoids the 6-day partial week and the 2.5x weekday/weekend effect.
NFR events (2%) excluded from all usage metrics.
Project environment = name-based rule (staging|qa|internal|sandbox|test|trial|eval + optional digits = non-prod). Shown alongside the label-based number where they differ.
Contract balance does not reconcile with usage; runway/exhaustion uses linear burn since starting_at and is an assumption.
Low-balance thresholds: 0.15 for credit and postpaid, 0.20 for prepaid, inferred from which alert the history attaches to each contract type.

CRM was profiled from SQLite directly. The tool must use the HTTP API: missing values come back as null (not absent); meeting contactIds is always []; type-specific fields only appear on their activity type; opportunities need one call per account.
All timestamps in both sources are 08:00:00.000Z, so day granularity only.
The 16 ambiguous accounts have no usage fields in the preview, by design. The 8 unmatched tenants are outside the preview.
Flags are independent booleans, not a score; counts are of the 200 accounts (184 resolvable).
Synthetic data: tenants cust_001-021 (region NULL) carry the hand-made stories (special project names, notes, meetings). The rest look randomly generated, so don't overfit thresholds to them.
